title: cymbopogon exaltatus var. ambiguus
intro: Cymbopogon exaltatus var. ambiguus, commonly known as East Indian lemon grass, is a type of aromatic grass native to tropical regions. This plant is prized for its health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which can help to reduce stress and alleviate symptoms of digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of East Indian lemon grass include its ability to act as an antiseptic, an antispasmodic, and a diuretic, making it useful in treating a range of conditions from skin irritations to urinary tract infections. The bioactive constituents of East Indian lemon grass include citral, limonene, and beta-pinene, which are responsible for its distinct lemon-like aroma and its various therapeutic properties.
